treaty_name: Convention between the Government of Canada and the Government of the State of Israel for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (2016)
eif_quote: [Note: Notice given that the Convention entered into force on December 21, 2016, see Canada Gazette Part I, Volume 151, page 664.] | Art. 28(1)(a): (a) in respect of taxes withheld at source, on amounts paid or credited to non-residents, on or after the first day of January of the calendar year following that in which this Convention enters into force; and
source_title: Canada–Israel Tax Convention Act, 2016, Schedule — consolidated, Justice Laws Website

rates.quote: (a) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a company (other than a partnership) which holds directly at least 25 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends;
(b) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

2 However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

2 However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude; having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement. [Canada notified Arts. 10(10), 11(10), 12(8), 13(7) of this treaty as existing provisions described in MLI Art. 7(2).]

notes: MLI Art. 8 applies: Canada (no. 33) and Israel (no. 8) both notified Art. 10(2)(a); Israel’s Art. 8(3)(b)(iii) reservation lists only the US treaty. From 2020-01-01 the 25% holding must be met throughout a 365-day period. Not modelled: Art. 11(3)(f) 5% cap on arm’s-length interest beneficially owned by a financial institution (bank-only tier): (f) the tax charged by a Contracting State on interest arising in that State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the interest if the beneficial owner of the interest is a financial institution and is dealing at arm’s length with the payer. Art. 10(3)/11(3)(a)-(b): government/central-bank exemptions; Art. 10(4)/11(3)(e): recognized pension organisations exempt; Art. 11(3)(c)-(d): EDC/ASHRA arm’s-length loans exempt. Art. 12(3): copyright (excl. film/TV), computer software, patent and know-how royalties taxable only in residence State. Treaty main-purpose rules Arts. 10(10), 11(10), 12(8). Branch tax max 5% (Art. 10(9)).
